issues.description: Command naming inconsistent with sibling commands (quickmark_save, bookmark_add use singular).
issues.detail: Existing commands use singular forms: quickmark_save, quickmark_load, bookmark_add, bookmark_load. The new commands use plural quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload. This breaks the discoverability invariant of the command namespace. A reader scanning :quickmark-<TAB> would not find the reload. Pick one convention.

issues.description: reload() leaves marks partially mutated if _parse_line raises mid-file.
issues.detail: The invariant should be: after reload(), self.marks reflects exactly the on-disk file, or is unchanged. The implementation clears first, then parses line by line; a malformed line raising InvalidUrlError mid-file leaves marks in a half-loaded state and still emits changed. Parse into a local OrderedDict, then swap atomically.

issues.description: reload() always emits changed even when contents are identical.
issues.detail: If the on-disk file is unchanged, reload() still emits self.changed, forcing any observer (completion model, UI) to re-render. Cheap to compare old vs. new OrderedDict before emitting. Not asymptotically wrong, but a wasted notification on the hot path of repeated reloads.

issues.description: Test does not verify the failure mode it implies it covers.
issues.detail: test_reload exercises the happy path but never asserts the invariant under a malformed second file, nor that marks survives unchanged on parse failure. Given reload() is the whole point of the PR, one negative test (malformed line on reload) would catch the partial-mutation bug above. A proof would be better; a test is what we have.

issues.description: Two new BDD scenarios lack scenario titles.
issues.detail: Both new entries are written as bare `Scenario:` with no name. Every other scenario in the file is titled (`Scenario: Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)`). Readability of the feature file matters; an untitled scenario is harder to locate in failure output. Name them e.g. `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks (:bookmarks-reload)`.

issues.description: _init_lineparser is now called twice on construction.
issues.detail: __init__ calls self.reload(), which calls self._init_lineparser(). Previously _init_lineparser ran once at construction. Not a correctness bug — the lineparser is idempotent — but the constructor's data flow is now less obvious to a reader. A one-line comment stating the invariant (`reload() establishes the initial in-memory state from disk`) would earn its keep.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The refactor of construction into reload() is the right shape — one method, one invariant: in-memory marks mirror the file on disk. But the invariant is not preserved under exceptions: clear() runs before parsing, so a malformed line on a subsequent reload leaves the manager in a half-loaded state and still emits `changed`. Parse into a local structure, then swap. Naming (`quickmarks_reload` vs. existing singular `quickmark_save`) is a discoverability regression worth fixing before merge. Tests cover the happy path only; the negative test that would catch the partial-mutation bug is missing.
